Neither a cancellation-installed nor worker-call-returned checkpoint was observed for the SQL negative. Because finish_by precedes its receipt write and diagnostics occur between receipts, missing receipt does not prove cancellation was never installed.

The busy negative did reach DatabaseBusy return at 4.043866s, stall marker at 4.0442271s, completion timeout and join-start, and actual root cleanup. It therefore independently supplies that real-call negative control despite slow setup.

The SQL-negative path already used the exact same open_shutdown_fixture before this health-only change. Reduced concurrent health setup cost is at most a hypothesis for indirect relief; no receipt proves it repairs the SQL-negative failure.
No evidence identifies Defender, fsync, disk, CPU, host contention, or a production cancellation regression as the root cause. The low-level Windows delay remains unresolved.
